bug_description.normalized: The saved 51-byte witness is accepted as a WAV IMA ADPCM file whose `fmt ` chunk materializes `format=WAVE_FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM`, `channels=1`, `blockalign=5`, and `samplesperblock=3`. `wavlike_read_fmt_chunk()` and `wav_read_header()` copy those values into `psf->sf.channels`, `psf->sf.format`, `blockalign`, and `framesperblock`; `wav_open()` and `wavlike_ima_init()` then forward them unchanged into `ima_reader_init()`. There, `pimasize = sizeof(IMA_ADPCM_PRIVATE) + blockalign * psf->sf.channels + 3 * psf->sf.channels * samplesperblock` budgets only 14 tail bytes even though the WAV decoder arm selected by `SF_CONTAINER (psf->sf.format)` will unpack this 5-byte mono block as one predictor plus 8 nibble slots. The existing consistency guard `samplesperblock == 2 * (blocksize - 4 * channels) / channels + 1` still holds for `5,1,3`, so `pima->decode_block` is bound to `wavlike_ima_decode_block()` and the first-block call proceeds on the undersized object. In `wavlike_ima_decode_block()`, the first out-of-bounds store is `pima->samples[7] = bytecode & 0x0F` at `src/ima_adpcm.c:432`; Stage 01's AddressSanitizer trace reports that 2-byte write exactly at the right edge of the 86-byte allocation from `ima_reader_init()`. The fix rounds the temporary decoded-sample count up to the decoder's 8-nibble granularity before calling `calloc`.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled WAV `fmt ` bytes and materializes the IMA ADPCM channel/block geometry later used by the vulnerable allocation and decoder.
source.value_from: In the exact 51-byte witness, these bytes decode as `format = 0x0011 (WAVE_FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM)`, `channels = 1`, `blockalign = 5`, and `bitwidth = 4`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. On the final inner-loop iteration for the witness block, `indx` becomes 7 and this 2-byte store lands at the first byte beyond the 86-byte heap allocation created in `ima_reader_init()`.
sink.note: Stage 01's ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 2` at `src/ima_adpcm.c:432` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 86-byte region allocated in `ima_reader_init()`.

root_cause.code: pimasize = sizeof (IMA_ADPCM_PRIVATE) + blockalign * psf->sf.channels + 3 * psf->sf.channels * samplesperblock ;
root_cause.description: The allocation-size formula underestimates the scratch space needed by `wavlike_ima_decode_block()`: it sizes the flexible-array tail directly from `blockalign` and `samplesperblock`, but the decoder unpacks WAV IMA blocks in 8-nibble groups and can therefore require more temporary `short` slots than this formula reserves.
root_cause.note: For the witness values `blockalign=5`, `channels=1`, and `samplesperblock=3`, this computes `sizeof(IMA_ADPCM_PRIVATE) + 14`. The patch adds the missing rounded-up count `((samplesperblock - 2) | 7) + 2`, which is 9 here, and sizes the allocation from that count instead.

parser_admitted.description: The witness survives the WAV IMA consistency checks, `wav_open()` forwards `blockalign=5` and `framesperblock=3` into `ima_reader_init()`, and the WAV container arm selected from `psf->sf.format` binds `pima->decode_block` to `wavlike_ima_decode_block()` before line 244 invokes the vulnerable first-block decoder.

tainted_value_origin.description: The IMA-specific extension fields complete the vulnerable block geometry. For the exact witness, this reads `samplesperblock=3`, the value later reused by both the allocation-size formula and the `samplesperblock != count` guard.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the exact witness, the `fmt ` chunk bytes `05 00 04 00 20 20 03 00` encode `blockalign=5`, `bitwidth=4`, `extrabytes=0x2020`, and `samplesperblock=3`.

coarse_trace.summary: The WAV header parser reads attacker-controlled IMA ADPCM fields and stores `channels=1`, `blockalign=5`, `samplesperblock=3`, and the IMA format tag into `psf` state and `wav_read_header()` outputs.
The forwarded `blockalign`/`framesperblock` locals and `psf->sf.channels` reach `ima_reader_init()`, where `pimasize` is computed too small and `calloc` allocates an undersized decoder object.
The present WAV IMA consistency check still accepts `blocksize=5`, `channels=1`, and `samplesperblock=3`, and the WAV container arm binds `pima->decode_block` to `wavlike_ima_decode_block()`.
The mono unpack loop expands the first 5-byte block as one predictor plus 8 nibble slots, so writing `pima->samples[7]` overruns the 86-byte allocation and triggers ASan.

fine_trace.note: Source. The WAV `fmt ` parser reads the attacker-controlled header into `wav_fmt`. For the exact 51-byte witness this materializes `format = WAVE_FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM`, `channels = 1`, `blockalign = 5`, and `bitwidth = 4`.

The IMA-specific extension fields are read next. The witness sets `samplesperblock = 3`; the only local rejection here is `samplesperblock < 1`, so this small frame count remains live for the later IMA reader setup.
The parsed channel count is copied into `psf->sf.channels`. The witness makes the decoder state mono (`1`), and this exact value is later multiplied into both `pimasize` and the unpack indices.

When `wav_fmt->format` is `WAVE_FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM`, `wav_read_header()` converts that tag into libsndfile's combined WAV-container/IMA-codec format. This value later drives both `SF_CODEC (psf->sf.format)` in `wav_open()` and `SF_CONTAINER (psf->sf.format)` in `ima_reader_init()`.

The same union-backed header field previously read as `wav_fmt->min.blockalign` is forwarded into `wav_read_header()`'s `blockalign` output. For the witness this preserves `blockalign = 5` for the later IMA initializer.
The parsed IMA frame count is forwarded out of `wav_read_header()`. For the witness this preserves `framesperblock = 3`.

fine_trace.code:
case SF_FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM :
					error = wavlike_ima_init (psf, blockalign, framesperblock) ;
fine_trace.note: After `subformat = SF_CODEC (psf->sf.format)` resolves to `SF_FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM`, `wav_open()` selects this case and passes the forwarded witness values `blockalign = 5` and `framesperblock = 3` into `wavlike_ima_init()`.

fine_trace.code:
if (psf->file.mode == SFM_READ)
		if ((error = ima_reader_init (psf, blockalign, samplesperblock)))
fine_trace.note: In read mode, the IMA wrapper forwards the same `blockalign` value and the `framesperblock` argument renamed as `samplesperblock` into `ima_reader_init()` without rewriting them.

fine_trace.code: pimasize = sizeof (IMA_ADPCM_PRIVATE) + blockalign * psf->sf.channels + 3 * psf->sf.channels * samplesperblock ;
fine_trace.note: Root cause. After the forwarded witness values reach `ima_reader_init()`, this formula uses `blockalign = 5`, `psf->sf.channels = 1`, and `samplesperblock = 3`, so the variable tail budget becomes only 14 bytes. The fix shows the missing obligation: scratch space must be rounded up to `((samplesperblock - 2) | 7) + 2`, which is 9 here.
This materializes the undersized decoder object from step 9. Stage 01's ASan trace records the resulting allocation as the 86-byte heap region later overflowed at its right edge.

The new object aliases both work buffers inside the same flexible-array tail: `samples` starts at `pima->data`, `block` starts after `samplesperblock * channels = 3` `short` slots, and the live decoder state becomes `channels = 1`, `blocksize = 5`, and `samplesperblock = 3`. Because step 10 allocated only 14 tail bytes total, the tail contains only 7 valid `short` slots (`samples[0]` through `samples[6]`) before the heap boundary.

Present guard. For the witness values this computes `count = 2 * (5 - 4 * 1) / 1 + 1 = 3`, so `pima->samplesperblock != count` is false and the block is accepted as internally consistent. There is still no guard that ties the tail from step 11 to the unpack loop's 8-nibble granularity.

Because step 4 made `SF_CONTAINER (psf->sf.format)` equal `SF_FORMAT_WAV`, `ima_reader_init()` stays in the WAV/W64 arm after step 12 and binds the first-block callback at line 244 to `wavlike_ima_decode_block()`.

The first-block call at line 244 now resolves to `wavlike_ima_decode_block()`. With `channels = 1`, the function has already stored the predictor at `pima->samples[0]`, then starts `blockindx = 4` and `indxstart = 1`; since `4 < blocksize (5)`, the fixed `for (k = 0 ; k < 4 ; k++)` loop writes nibble slots at indices `1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8`, so this decode path needs 9 `short` positions in total.

Sink. On the final inner-loop iteration (`k = 3`), step 14 makes `indx = 7`. Step 11's 14-byte tail provides valid `short` slots only through `samples[6]`, so this 2-byte store is the first write past the 86-byte allocation that ASan reports.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Parsed from the staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, and the preserved vulnerable source tree.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix changes only `ima_reader_init()`'s size calculation, adding a rounded temporary-sample count before `calloc`, which removes the write past the decoder allocation on this witness.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the saved ASan crash on the staged 51-byte RIFF/WAVE witness. Its `fmt ` chunk makes the file enter the WAV IMA ADPCM path with `channels=1`, `blockalign=5`, and `samplesperblock=3`, so `ima_reader_init()` allocates from those exact values and the first `wavlike_ima_decode_block()` call overflows at `pima->samples[7]`.

format.name: 51-byte RIFF/WAVE IMA ADPCM file
format.contract: Exactly these 51 bytes: `52 49 46 46 20 20 20 20 57 41 56 45 66 6d 74 20 15 00 00 00 11 00 01 00 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff ff 05 00 04 00 20 20 03 00 20 20 64 61 74 61 20 20 20 20 20`. The vulnerable parser reads this witness as a WAV IMA ADPCM file whose relevant header geometry is `channels=1`, `blockalign=5`, and `samplesperblock=3`, then crashes in the first `wavlike_ima_decode_block()` call. This contract is intentionally limited to the exact staged witness and observed crash; the staged artifacts do not establish a broader family of `blockalign`/`samplesperblock` combinations that reproduce the same overwrite.
